text:
**U.S. assembly‑plant start‑up dates for the three brands**

| Brand | First U.S. vehicle‑assembly plant | Opening year (first vehicle produced) | Source |
|-------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------|
| **Nissan** (including its Acura line) | **Smyrna, Tennessee** – the Nissan Smyrna Assembly Plant (first U.S. plant owned by Nissan) | **June 16 1983** – first Nissan pickup rolled off the line | [Wikipedia – Nissan Smyrna Assembly Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nissan_Smyrna_Assembly_Plant) |
| **Honda** (Acura Legend maker) | **Marysville, Ohio** – the Honda of America Mfg., Inc. auto plant (first U.S. plant owned by Honda) | **1979** – the company opened the plant in Marysville for its first U.S. automobile production (the Accord/Acura Legend) | [Honda U.S. Manufacturing](https://www.hondainamerica.com/u-s-manufacturing/) |
| **Toyota** (top‑selling U.S. brand) | **Georgetown, Kentucky** – Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky (first stand‑alone Toyota U.S. plant; NUMMI, the GM/Toyota joint‑venture, opened earlier in 1984 but was not a Toyota‑only plant) | **May 26 1988** – first Toyota/​Camry rolled off the line | [Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky – Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_Motor_Manufacturing_Kentucky) |

> *Note*: Toyota’s first U.S. assembly activity began in 1984 with the NUMMI joint‑venture in Fremont, CA. However, the first **Toyota‑owned, standalone U.S. assembly plant** began producing vehicles in 1988 in Georgetown, Kentucky.

These dates mark the birth of each brand’s domestic manufacturing footprint in the United States.
